According to the latest report from Counterpoint Research, even as the overall industry slumped, Apple's iPhone shipments still grew 3% year-over-year, setting a record with a 20% share of global smartphone shipments. Details are as follows.

Second-lowest quarterly level since 2013

Counterpoint Research said that during the second quarter of 2026, Samsung led the global smartphone market with a 24% shipment share, followed closely by Apple (20% share, a record for the quarter), Xiaomi (12%), OPPO (11%) and vivo (8%).

Compared with the same period last year, Samsung's share rose by 4 percentage points, Apple rose by 3 percentage points, vivo rose by 1 percentage point, Xiaomi fell by 2 percentage points, and OPPO fell by 1 percentage point. The combined share of other manufacturers dropped from 28% to 26%.

Counterpoint noted that Samsung returned to the top of the global smartphone shipment rankings in the second quarter of 2026, after Apple had taken the lead in the first quarter on the back of strong demand for the iPhone 17.

As for the second quarter of 2026, although Apple was the only major OEM to avoid raising prices, Samsung benefited from strong demand for the Galaxy S26 series, improved product supply, and a more aggressive promotional strategy, growing at a faster pace.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects "global smartphone shipments to decline by around 14% for the full year, with the global memory shortage expected to persist into 2027." The firm noted that manufacturers will continue to cut low-margin models, adjust storage configurations, and rely more heavily on refurbished and previous-generation products until supply conditions improve.
